title: The knob surface's reply
description: How the declared values stand now, and what was done with the most recent write. **The declarations themselves — ranges and choices — come along**, so a reader never goes to another surface to find out what can be written. Rewritten at launch, when a write is answered, and when a value actually changes.

revision.description: A number that advances whenever the contents change. **It advances on launch alone**, because a new process can change the declarations themselves: how many knobs there are, their ranges, their choices. A reader tells whether its own copy is stale by this.

id.description: The identifier of the most recent request answered. Omitted when none has been answered yet. **Echoed even when nothing went in**, so that everything being refused is told apart from nothing arriving.

params.description: The declared values. **The order is the order they were written in**, from the base upward, and that order is part of what the surface says.

value.description: The value now. Its type is what this declaration's type says.

min.description: The lower end of the range it can move in. If absent, no range was declared. **Whether a knob appears is decided by the type** — numbers and tuples (float, int, vec2, vec3) get no knob in the window without a declared range, though they can still be written from outside, while booleans and colours appear regardless of this key, and for strings it is choices that decides.

max.description: The upper end of the range it can move in.

choices.description: The choices that are allowed. The legal values are on the surface, so a writer never has to try them all.

rejected.description: The writes that did not go in, and why. An empty array when nothing was refused.

reason.description: unknownName = a name that was never declared (check the spelling) / typeMismatch = a type other than the declared one / notInChoices = outside the choices that are allowed.

clamped.description: The writes that went in after being brought into range. **Bringing them in is never done in silence**, so that the gap between what was written and what reads back has a reason. An empty array when nothing was brought in.

requested.description: The value the writer asked for.

value.description: The value that actually went in.

discarded.description: Saved values that were thrown away for not matching the declarations. **This can only fill at launch** — change a declaration by renaming it, changing its type, or narrowing its choices, and the saved value can no longer be taken. Throwing them away in silence would look like nothing but values mysteriously returning to their defaults. An empty array when nothing was thrown away.

reason.description: unknownName = a name that was never declared (check the spelling) / typeMismatch = a type other than the declared one / notInChoices = outside the choices that are allowed.
